fact: When a diagnostic export (e.g. C_qn_fast_orig, rob_loc_fast_orig) is removed after its optimization phase, remove all skip_if_not(exists('export_name')) test blocks at the same commit.
why: Tests guarded by a missing export become permanently-skipped dead code that accumulates as CI SKIP noise and obscures real skip signals. The removal commit is the right moment — context is fresh and the tests can never run again.

fact: To exclude dev-tooling dirs (.beads/, .metaswarm/, .tldr/) from R packages: (1) add entries to .Rbuildignore so they are excluded from the build tarball; (2) run git rm --cached -r <dir> for any dir that was committed before the .gitignore entry existed.
why: .Rbuildignore fixes R CMD check NOTEs about hidden/non-standard files by keeping them out of the tarball. git rm --cached is separately needed to stop git tracking files that predate their .gitignore entry — both steps are required.

fact: When an estimator calls median selection TWICE (median + MAD), calling both implementations twice preserves the ratio — the crossover threshold does NOT shift. No separate constant is needed for the double-call case; the same threshold applies.
why: WU-RS3: rob_scale_core calls median/MAD selection twice per invocation. Theoretical analysis: sort_network(n=16)~46 ops vs FR(n=16)~16 ops; doubling both preserves ratio. Empirical confirmation impossible at sub-µs scale (timer quantum dominates).

fact: When a DoD item explicitly states 'all call sites of X updated (grep to confirm)', the effective file scope extends to wherever those call sites exist — even files not in the declared scope. The DoD is the authoritative spec; file scope is a constraint but explicit DoD call-site requirements take precedence.
why: WU-CLEAN-2 declared iqr.cpp and estimators_internal.h as file scope, but the DoD said 'all call sites of iqr() updated (grep to confirm)'. The sole external call site was in ensemble.cpp. Updating ensemble.cpp was required to satisfy the DoD; restricting to declared scope would have left a broken call.

fact: For fork-based parallelism (mclapply) in benchmark pipelines, cap workers with safe_worker_count(): min(n_phys-1, floor(avail_mb * 0.80 / worker_mem_mb)). Default the hard cap to n_phys-1 (not a fixed number like 4) and let the memory formula be the binding constraint. Override via BENCH_MAX_WORKERS env var for CI. Emit INFO/WARN lines so resource decisions are visible in the pipeline log.
why: A fixed cap of 4 wastes 12 idle cores on a 16-core machine with 11 GB free. A cap of n_phys crashes the same machine when 9 GB of swap is already in use. The memory formula adapts to actual conditions at runtime.

fact: When a plan claims an iteration converges at a specific rate (linear/quadratic), verify the claim against the actual denominator before accepting the plan. Fixed denominator = IRLS (linear, |T'(t*)|<1). Observed/data-dependent denominator = NR (quadratic, T'(t*)=0). This determines whether acceleration methods like Aitken or Steffensen apply.
why: The robLoc Aitken plan required 4 gate iterations (beyond the 3-iteration official max) because the convergence-rate claim (T'(t*)≈−0.57, linear IRLS) was wrong. The code used the observed Hessian (NR, quadratic). The gate's Feasibility reviewer checked file paths but not the algorithmic premise; empirical testing caught it instead.

fact: After removing a diagnostic export, add expect_false(exists('export_name', envir = asNamespace('pkg'), inherits = FALSE)) tests. Unlike skip-guarded tests removed at cleanup time, absence-assertion guards persist permanently and fail immediately if the export is re-added.
why: pattern-diagnostic-export-lifecycle removes skip-guarded tests at cleanup. Absence guards complement this: they survive the cleanup commit and enforce the removed state across all future sessions. Used for rob_scale_nr_impl and rob_scale_nr_iters in test-robscale-nr.R.
